stem: Which of the following are true about the relationship between a single reflection pass and a multi-round self-critique loop? (Select 2)

options.text: A self-critique loop is essentially multiple reflection-and-revision rounds chained together
A single reflection pass can only ever be used on the very first draft of an output
Both approaches aim to catch issues in a candidate output before it's finalized
A self-critique loop guarantees strictly better output than a single reflection pass on every task

explanation.why_correct: A self-critique loop extends the basic idea of reflection into multiple chained rounds, and both approaches share the same underlying goal of catching and fixing issues before finalizing an output.

why_incorrect.B: A single reflection pass can be applied to any candidate output at any stage, not only a first draft.
why_incorrect.D: Due to diminishing returns, additional rounds don't guarantee strictly better results on every task; sometimes a single well-executed reflection pass is sufficient and additional rounds add cost with little gain.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Self-critique loops generalize single-pass reflection into multiple rounds, but more rounds are not automatically guaranteed to be strictly better due to diminishing returns.

stem: A developer wants to add reflection to a system but is worried about added latency for every single request, including very simple ones. What is a reasonable design response to this concern?

options.text: Apply reflection selectively, e.g. for complex or high-stakes outputs, rather than unconditionally on every request
Remove all reasoning from the system entirely
Apply exactly 20 rounds of self-critique to every request without exception
Ignore the latency concern since it is never a legitimate consideration

explanation.why_correct: Selectively applying reflection to complex or high-stakes outputs (where its benefit is more likely to outweigh its cost) while skipping it for simple, low-stakes requests is a reasonable way to balance quality against latency.

why_incorrect.B: Removing all reasoning is a drastic, unrelated overreaction that would harm quality broadly, not a targeted response to the latency concern about reflection specifically.
why_incorrect.C: Applying a large fixed number of critique rounds to every request, including simple ones, would make the latency problem worse, not better.
why_incorrect.D: Latency is a legitimate, practical engineering concern; dismissing it outright ignores real tradeoffs that matter for usability and cost.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Reflection's cost-benefit tradeoff favors selective application to complex or high-stakes cases, rather than uniform application to every request regardless of need.

stem: Which statement most accurately summarizes the value and limits of self-reflection together?

options.text: Self-reflection is useless and should never be used in any system
Self-reflection meaningfully helps catch certain error types (slips, requirement gaps, inconsistencies) but shares blind spots with the original generation for genuine knowledge gaps
Self-reflection is a complete substitute for all forms of external verification in every context
Self-reflection only works if a different company's model is used for the critique step

explanation.why_correct: This captures the balanced, accurate picture: self-reflection has genuine value for certain error types, but it is not a cure-all, since it shares the same underlying knowledge-based blind spots as the original generation.

why_incorrect.A: Dismissing self-reflection as useless ignores its real, demonstrated value for catching slips, requirement gaps, and logical inconsistencies.
why_incorrect.C: Self-reflection cannot fully substitute for external verification precisely because of its shared blind-spot limitation for genuine knowledge gaps.
why_incorrect.D: Using a different company's model is not a stated requirement for reflection to provide value; the same model can serve both generation and critique roles, with the limitation being about shared knowledge, not company origin.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Self-reflection is genuinely useful but not a complete solution -- it needs to be paired with external verification for the error types it cannot catch.
